title: The Nuclear IPO Boom Is Back: How Westinghouse and Its Rivals Stack Up for Long-Term Investors
author: Nicholas Sciple, Jim Gillies, And Lou Whiteman
description: A new wave of nuclear IPOs is emerging, ranging from established operators like Westinghouse to highly speculative start-ups. Investors should carefully evaluate sponsor quality, cash runway, and revenue visibility when considering nuclear IPO investments, as the sector presents both solid opportunities and significant risks.

title: This Newly Public Nuclear IPO Is Already Using AI to Speed Up Reactor Design. Is It a Buy?
author: Jeff Siegel
description: X-Energy, a newly public nuclear company, is leveraging AI through Project Prometheus to accelerate reactor design, licensing, and manufacturing. With major customers like Amazon, Dow Inc., and Centrica, plus an 11.5-gigawatt pipeline, the company has strong tailwinds but faces significant execution risks in licensing, construction, and financing.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Company is positioned at intersection of AI and nuclear power trends, has $1.9B in liquidity with no debt, secured major customers (Amazon, Dow, Centrica), and is using AI to potentially reduce development timelines and costs. However, author notes it's a high-risk growth stock requiring successful execution.
Amazon is backing nuclear projects with X-Energy and Energy Northwest, with potential to support over 5 gigawatts by 2039, positioning itself as a major driver of AI data center power demand.
Nvidia is a founding member of Project Prometheus, contributing expertise to integrate AI models into nuclear reactor development and operations.
Dow is collaborating with X-Energy on a four-reactor project but this represents a customer relationship rather than direct investment thesis.
Centrica is exploring potential nuclear projects with X-Energy in the U.K. but represents early-stage partnership with uncertain outcomes.

title: Palantir Billionaire Peter Thiel Just Put 33% of His Portfolio Into These 3 Energy Stocks
author: Adam Spatacco
description: Peter Thiel's hedge fund Thiel Macro rebuilt a $419 million portfolio in Q2 2026, allocating roughly 33% across three energy stocks: Vista Energy, Vistra, and X-Energy. Thiel views electricity as the critical bottleneck for AI development rather than chips, positioning in nuclear and energy infrastructure to enable AI hyperscaler operations.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Thiel invested $76 million (18% of fund), positioning it as Argentina's leading independent energy producer. Investment appears driven by confidence in President Milei's deregulation and reform policies unlocking hydrocarbon basin potential.

Thiel allocated $59 million (14% of fund) to this nuclear power operator. Company has secured 20-year power agreements with AWS and Meta, and participates in Helix venture with Nvidia and KKR, positioning it as key enabler of AI workloads requiring 24/7 carbon-free baseload power.

Smallest position at ~1% of portfolio despite Amazon backing. While representing the nuclear-AI theme, the minimal allocation suggests Thiel's modest assessment of this particular AI narrative and SMR technology's near-term impact.

Largest position in Thiel Macro's portfolio. Major customer of nuclear power providers (AWS power agreements with Vistra) and backer of X-Energy, indicating Thiel's confidence in Amazon's AI infrastructure strategy.

title: Oklo Vs. X-Energy: Is the New Nuclear IPO the Better Buy?
author: John Bromels
description: Oklo and X-Energy are competing small modular reactor (SMR) companies with different technological approaches. Both are pre-commercial, highly speculative investments with no guaranteed regulatory approval. Oklo appears slightly ahead in development timeline, making it the marginally better choice between two risky bets.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Described as 'the better buy' of the two companies due to being further along in development process with first reactor expected to reach criticality around Q1 2027. Has backing from Sam Altman and support from Trump administration.

Comparable technology and backing (Amazon partnership, DOE support) but appears slightly behind Oklo in development timeline with construction unlikely to begin until Q1 2027. Regulatory review still ongoing.

title: Why Cameco's Ugly Earnings Miss Might Be Good News in Disguise
author: Matt Dilallo
description: Cameco reported disappointing Q2 earnings with revenue down 7% and EPS missing estimates significantly, but the miss was largely due to lower equity earnings from its Westinghouse investment. As Westinghouse prepares for an IPO, the investment could unlock substantial value for Cameco shareholders, with Westinghouse's valuation estimated to have grown from CA$8.2 billion to CA$10.8 billion since Cameco's 2023 acquisition of a 49% stake.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Despite missing earnings expectations, the underlying business fundamentals appear sound. The earnings miss was attributed to accounting treatment of Westinghouse investment rather than core business weakness. The potential IPO of Westinghouse could unlock significant hidden value, with the investment growing substantially in valuation since acquisition.

As co-owner of Westinghouse with a 51% stake, Brookfield Renewable stands to benefit from the upcoming IPO and value unlock similar to Cameco. The global nuclear resurgence has increased Westinghouse's valuation.

While X-Energy successfully completed its IPO in April 2026 raising over $1 billion, initial enthusiasm has cooled significantly. The stock initially popped 27% but is now marginally down from its IPO price, suggesting market sentiment for nuclear IPOs is mixed.

Standard Nuclear's IPO performance has been poor, slumping 10% on debut and declining more than 45% from its IPO price. This weak performance could give Westinghouse pause regarding its own IPO timing and could negatively impact investor appetite for nuclear sector IPOs.
